text: Zhang Xiang JP (Chinese: 张翔; pinyin: Zhāng Xiáng; born December 1963) is a Chinese-American mechanical engineer who has served as the 16th president and vice-chancellor of the University of Hong Kong since July 2018. He was the inaugural Ernest S. Kuh Endowed Chaired Professor at the University of California, Berkeley, served as director of the National Science Foundation Nano-scale Science and Engineering Center, directed the materials science division, and held the position of senior faculty scientist at the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. Zhang earned a Bachelor of Science and a Master of Science from Nanjing University, a Master of Science from the University of Minnesota, and a Doctor of Philosophy from the University of California, Berkeley in 1996. From 1996 to 1999, he was an assistant professor at Pennsylvania State University, and from 1999 to 2004, he held positions as associate professor and then full professor at the University of California, Los Angeles, before joining UC Berkeley. He is an elected member of the United States National Academy of Engineering and Academia Sinica, a foreign member of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and a Fellow of the American Physical Society, the Optical Society of America (OSA), the American Association for the Advancement of Science, and the International Society for Optical Engineering. Zhang has published more than 390 journal papers, with research focusing on materials physics, metamaterials, and nano-photonics. On 15 December 2017, The University of Hong Kong appointed Zhang to the roles of president and vice-chancellor, marking the first time a candidate born and educated to undergraduate degree level in mainland China had been appointed to such a position; he assumed office in July 2018. On 3 July 2019, in response to the Storming of the Legislative Council Complex two days earlier, Zhang stated he was "disheartened by the violence" and that he "would like to condemn such acts"; in response to backlash from approximately 2,000 HKU students, alumni, and staff, he affirmed on 11 July that he opposed violence "by any party, and at any juncture" and agreed to participate in a forum open to students, staff, alumni, and the media. In April 2021, the Hong Kong University Students' Union criticized Zhang, claiming he was promoting national security education as a "political task" and was "destroying the autonomy of institutions." In October 2023, Zhang was accused by whistleblowers of potential misconduct, including the purchase of a HK$2 million (US$255,370) BMW vehicle without going through an open tender.
